The first-generation Apple TV 4K launched in 2017 has just been added to Apple's "vintage" product list. Here's what this classification means.

The first-generation Apple TV 4K has been classified as "vintage," and repair services may be reduced

If you're still using the first-generation Apple TV 4K, launched nearly a decade ago, getting it repaired may become more complicated.

As discovered by MacRumors, Apple has marked the first-generation Apple TV 4K as "vintage."

Apple maintains lists of vintage and obsolete products on its website.

  • "Vintage" means the product has been out of sale for more than five years
  • "Obsolete" means it has been out of sale for more than seven years

If a product is marked as "obsolete," Apple will completely cease providing service or hardware repairs.

If it's "vintage," in most cases Apple can still provide repair services, though it depends on parts availability.

So if you still have a first-generation Apple TV 4K and might need repairs, it's best to take care of it soon. Alternatively, you can keep an eye out for the new Apple TV 4K announced at next week's "Welcome Home" event.

Are you still using the first-generation Apple TV 4K? Feel free to share in the comments.
